teams.heading: FRU chairman John Sanday says Solomon Islands want into Fiji domestic competitions
teams.body: Fiji's domestic club rugby is drawing regional suitors. Sanday told the Fiji Sun that Solomon Islands are "excited about the idea" and talks are planned when their Usotasi club visits for the Nadi junior tournament in early December. A Tonga official raised the idea at the Skipper Cup final, France has pitched Wallis & Futuna, New Caledonia and Tahiti, and three Papua New Guinea unions, frustrated by PNG's World Rugby suspension, asked to join FRU.

lead.why: The Santamaria and Marin stories have already run and the Dubai item is sevens, so the freshest Fiji event is FRU's regional expansion talks.

teams.heading: England risk fine for drafting Lewis Moody to face All Blacks' haka
teams.body: The Sun reports that England's decision to bring Rugby World Cup winner Moody in to face New Zealand's haka could cost them a fine. Today's press does not say who would impose it or how much it might be. The row comes before Saturday's rematch at Allianz Stadium, where England meet the All Blacks for third place in the Nations Championship finals weekend. Borthwick's side won the Round 6 meeting 37-12, which Matt Dawson's BBC column called a record win for a northern hemisphere side over New Zealand.

lead.why: The only new England story today, and a talking point a fan would pass on before the rematch.

teams.heading: Philippe Sella edges Jean-Pierre Rives to win the Jauréguy-Dominici prize
teams.body: France's 111-cap centre was chosen in Paris on Tuesday by a jury of journalists, former players and rugby figures, and the vote was tight between him and Jean-Pierre Rives. The ceremony fell on the anniversary of Christophe Dominici's death. The prize was created in 1980 to honour Franco-British rugby ties. It lapsed after 1997 and was revived two years ago with a wider brief. Sella fits the original purpose: he was the first French player in the English league, with Saracens from 1996 to 1998.

lead.why: Moefana's interview has already run, so this is the freshest reported event about France ahead of opinion pieces and Springbok-side news.

teams.heading: Former Ireland U20 Noah Byrne rejects Leinster, signs AFL deal with Brisbane
teams.body: Former Ireland U20 international Noah Byrne is heading for Australian Rules. The 20-year-old has signed a Category B contract with three-time AFL champions Brisbane Lions, sealing a move that looked likely once he turned down a professional deal with Leinster in the summer. Byrne came through Gonzaga College and Trinity College and started every one of Ireland's games in this year's U20 Six Nations. The42 calls the switch a blow to a province that rated him a serious prospect.

lead.why: Sheehan's ban has already run today, so the strongest fresh Ireland event is a U20 international leaving rugby for the AFL, reported by two outlets.

teams.heading: Federico Ruzza thanks Udine fans as Italy fly out for Fiji rematch
teams.body: Italy wrapped up their Udine camp with a final session at the Stadio Otello Gerli, home of Rugby Udine, before supporters came to meet the squad ahead of this morning's flight to London. Federico Ruzza called it always a pleasure to meet such affectionate fans, singling out the children who came for a greeting or a hug, and thanked Rugby Udine for its welcome. The Twickenham rematch with Fiji decides 11th place, and a win would end a seven-match losing run.

lead.why: The only new senior-men's Italy item; the Santamaria breakdown story and the Zambonin and Lynagh call-ups have already run, and the ItalSeven item is sevens.

teams.heading: Scotland release Duhan van der Merwe; Matt Fagerson out of Argentina finale
teams.body: Scotland have sent Duhan van der Merwe back to Edinburgh before the fourth-place final against Argentina at Twickenham. The 31-year-old winger did not feature in any of the three Murrayfield games this month. Matt Fagerson is also ruled out with a jaw injury from the 67-5 win over Japan, having started against New Zealand and Australia before being promoted from the bench when Rory Darge withdrew. Tuesday's squad update made no mention of Nathan McBeth, forced off with an ankle injury against the Brave Blossoms.

lead.why: A fresh Scotland squad update with a release and an injury blow before the Argentina finale.

teams.heading: WalesOnline urges Tandy to hand Macs Page Test debut against Japan
teams.body: Steve Tandy is expected to ring the changes for Saturday's Nations Championship finale against Japan, and WalesOnline's Steffan Thomas argues that is the moment for the Scarlets' 21-year-old to make the step up. Page has drawn comparisons with Shane Williams; the staff are understood to want further development in his aerial game. Thomas concedes Ellis Mee and Tom Rogers may sit ahead of him in the pecking order, but argues Japan's fast, expansive style makes an ideal stage for a first taste of Test rugby.

lead.why: Unlike the already-run Edwards injury story, this is a new selection case for the senior side's coming Test against Japan.

teams.heading: Pumas get Frenchman Pierre Brousset for Scotland finale after Vivas red card
teams.body: Sunday's Twickenham meeting with Scotland will be refereed by Pierre Brousset, who handled the most recent Top 14 semi-final between Toulouse and Racing 92. Fellow Frenchmen Luc Ramos and Éric Gauzins join him as assistant referee and TMO respectively, with England's Christophe Ridley on the other touchline. Argentina arrive without Mayco Vivas, sent off in last Saturday's 45-17 defeat by France, a night on which Hollie Davidson was also left untangling a late Pumas replacement muddle involving Guido Petti.

teams.heading: Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii backs midfield role as Ireland lose banned Dan Sheehan
teams.body: Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii says he loves playing 13 because "you get to be both sides of the ball", and his return to centre has coincided with the Wallabies' uptick in form. Les Kiss used him on the wing in September's 42-38 win over South Africa, the first Bledisloe test and the heavy loss to England, before restoring him for Scotland and last weekend's 29-26 win over Wales. Ireland must reshape for the fifth-place play-off: stand-in captain Dan Sheehan is banned for two games, leaving a gap at No. 8.

lead.why: A fresh Australia selection storyline on Suaalii, framed with the Sheehan ban as Australia's boost rather than Ireland's problem.

teams.heading: Japan without Takeuchi, Tokito and Riley for Scotland's 67-5 Murrayfield rout
teams.body: Shuhei Takeuchi and Riku Tokito joined both props, Keijiro Tamafusa and Opeti Helu, on the sidelines through injury or condition, while centre Dylan Riley — described by Rugby Asia 247 as Japan's lynchpin — was absent for personal reasons. Toyota Verblitz's Taufa Latu was among those called up. The depleted squad arrived in Edinburgh a week after England's 78-15 win at Twickenham, and Eddie Jones' side conceded 24 tries across the two defeats.

lead.why: It is the highest-ranked Japan story left, and it covers the absentees behind the Murrayfield defeat.

teams.heading: Taine Randell blames loose forwards after England beat All Blacks 37-12
teams.body: Former All Blacks captain Taine Randell told The Platform NZ podcast he was "zero percent confident that we were going to get absolutely smoked" at Twickenham, which is exactly what England then did. The ex-back-row, who played 51 Tests between 1997 and 2002, said New Zealand's loose forwards no longer win the collision: "we just do not dominate the advantage line." He also pointed to what he calls "an obsession" in New Zealand with a flashy style of play, especially at Super Rugby level.

teams.heading: Schalk Burger backs Springboks' scrum and maul to beat France in final
teams.body: Burger used SuperSport's The Verdict to pick apart the attack in the 17-20 defeat by Ireland. He called it a late-season "blip" and warned "we’ve only got a maul and a scrum at the minute". Yet those weapons underpin his faith for Sunday's Nations Championship final rematch against France at Twickenham: "There's no answer for them to stop our scrum," he said. He cautioned that leaning on set piece leaves the Boks hostage to the referee, citing Andrea Piardi's handling of the Paris defeat.

lead.why: The top item ran in an earlier edition, and Burger's verdict is the strongest new South Africa-centred story ahead of the France final.
